title: Introduce lazy test initializer and dependency declutterer
author: Aisha K. Mendes
description: Motivation: CI latency and flakiness on presubmit lanes is a recurring drag on engineer feedback loops. This PR introduces a lazy test initializer that defers expensive per-test setup until the runtime actually requires it, combined with a dependency-declutter pipeline that prunes rarely used devdeps at build time. Goals: (1) reduce average presubmit walltime by ~20-30% for the Python and TypeScript stacks, (2) reduce toolchain install noise and transient version conflicts, (3) surface an automated dep-prune report for maintainers. Changes are implemented so they are opt-in via a lightweight flag in .github/workflows/presubmit.yml and default enabled for fastpath lanes. Checklist: - [x] Implement lazy initializer shim for pytest/xdist and Jest worker boot - [x] Add dependency declutter script and CI step that produces an actionable report - [x] Add integration tests for initializer behavior and a smoke job for the declutter pipeline - [x] Update docs and console runbook links - [x] Gradual rollout via feature flag in CI; tested on staging. Related: Linear ENG-1289 (CI fastpath improvements), ENG-1342 (dep hygiene backlog). See presubmit metrics snapshot: https://internal.redwood/ci/metrics/ENG-1289. This description is continuous: the PR also contains a small operator to fallback to the previous eager initializer if a runtime probe detects regressions, and a no-op path for repos that rely on non-standard test entrypoints.
